MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 16, 2015

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Schlicht at 5:00 p.m., on February 16, 2015, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 11, 2015, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Schlicht

Absent:  Council Member Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there are no Closed Session agenda items this evening.

RECESS

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Schlicht declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:00
p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

City Council Minutes  1  February 16, 2015
 INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Veterans of Foreign War Post 6024

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclamation Recognizing the 100th Birthday of Retired Rear Admiral Bill A. Miles

  Mayor Schlicht presented the proclamation to Admiral Bill A. Miles.

P2.  Presentation by the American Diabetes Association on the "Tour de Cure" Bike Race

  The City Council received the presentation from Associate Director Tamara Kenworthy
  from the American Diabetes Association.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Kevin Frabotta, General Manager of the Lake Mission Viejo Association, M.V.: updated the City
Council on the status of the golden algae outbreak at Lake Mission Viejo and reported that efforts
to address the problem seem to be working.

Lamar Kelsoe, M.V.: expressed his disappointment that three Council Members supported the
appointment of former Council Member Dave Leckness to the Planning and Transportation
Commission and he recalled a derogatory email that he received from Mr. Leckness.

Sara Gilliland, M.V.: discussed the positive impacts that the Nadadores programs have on
countless lives and she shared her experience with the Masters Diving Program. She stated that
the City needs the swim and dive facility to keep the community young and healthy.

Ron Ruef, M.V.: addressing item 19 which was tabled this evening, he offered to find out what
commissioners are getting paid in other cities. He noted that Mission Viejo commissions are
being asked to do more and more work and therefore he thinks it is appropriate to increase the
commissioners’ pay.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, 6, and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  2  February 16, 2015
 AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the Regular Meeting of February 2, 2015, as presented.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2014

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for December 2014

  Received and filed.

 9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  December 2014

  Received and filed.

 10.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for December 2014

  Received and filed.

 11.  Federal-Aid Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant: Citywide
  Emergency Vehicle Pre-emption (EVP) Installation Project (CIP 215)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion; (5) approved funding in the amount of $38,400
City Council Minutes  3  February 16, 2015
   for the installation of emergency vehicle pre-emption activators on the City's Orange
  County Sheriff's Department vehicles; and (6) adopted Resolution 15-07 Amending the
  Fiscal Year 2014-2015 Budget for Costs Related to Emergency Vehicle Pre-emption
  Activator Installation.

 13.  Claim Against the City - Anna Warner

  Rejected claim.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

 3.  Check Register Dated January 23, 2015 in the Amount of $1,910,671.79

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern with payments made to Jamey Clark for sign
  removal, new frames and concrete work in the amount of $1,900 and a $1,600 payment
  for pressure washing the rubber play area at Pavion Park.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the
  pressure wash was required to clean muddy areas after Eagle Scout volunteers did planting
  projects at the park and there were several rains. Mr. Rattay noted that the other payment
  to Jamey Clark was for replacement of a rusted sign, one new sign, and for routine
  maintenance.

  Mayor Schlicht asked why the City paid for miscellaneous plants for Montilla slopes and
  why staff chose that particular corner.

  Mr. Rattay responded that several residents expressed frustration and wanted the City to
  do something to improve the area. Staff felt that rehabilitating the corner was the right
  thing to do and the funding was available in the operating budget.
  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 4.  Check Register Dated January 30, 2015 in the Amount of $804,362.53

  Mayor Schlicht expressed concern with payments for about $3,000 for the Felipe Tennis
  Center. She stated that the Council prioritized CIPs and Felipe Tennis Center was put at
  the bottom.

City Council Minutes  4  February 16, 2015
   Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services stated that this work was engaged
  prior to the CIP prioritization conversation.
  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

 *Items 5 and 6 were considered together.

 5.  Review and Approval of the Successor Agency’s Administrative Budget for the 15-
  16A Six-Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2015 to December 31, 2015

 6.  Review and Approval of Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the Six-
  Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2015 to December 31, 2015 ("ROPS 15-16A")

  Treasury Manager Josey Julian presented the staff report and answered the Council
  Members' questions.

  Council Member Sachs stated that it is incumbent upon the City Council Members to
  understand how the Boards that they sit on work. He suggested that the Council Members
  meet with staff and ask questions so that they are well informed. He also expressed
  concern with the amount of money that is spent on attorney fees as it continues to eat at
  the account balance and turns into hundreds of thousands of dollars over time.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) adopt
  Successor Agency Resolution 15-01 Approving the Successor Agency’s Administrative
  Budget for the 15-16A Six-Month Fiscal Period of July 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015,
  Pursuant to Section 34177(j) of the Dissolution Law (Agenda Item 5,) and (2) adopt
  Successor Agency Resolution 15-02 Approving Recognized Obligation Payment
  Schedule for the six-month fiscal period of July 1, 2015 to December 31, 2015 (“ROPS
  15-16A”), subject to submittal to and review by the Oversight Board and then DOF.
  Further, the Administrative Services Director or her designee, in consultation with legal
  counsel, shall be authorized to request and complete meet and confer session(s) with the
  DOF and authorized to make augmentations, modifications, additions or revisions as may
  be necessary or directed by DOF (Agenda Item 6.)

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

City Council Minutes  5  February 16, 2015
  12.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Trabuco Road to Alicia
  Parkway - (CIP 221)

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff
  report.

  Mayor Schlicht stated that the original projected cost for this project was $514,848 and
  the budget has now increased by $269,000. She said that she cannot accept the bids and
  she asked her colleagues to reject them and fit the project to the budget, not the other way
  around.

  Mr. Rattay noted that the increased costs are due to an increase in plant materials and labor
  costs and going out for bid again will not necessarily result in lower bids and, in fact, the
  bids may be higher.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  reject the bid submitted by Green Giant Landscape, Inc.; (2) award a construction contract
  to Kasa Construction, Inc.(A15-05) for the Marguerite Parkway Median Island
  Improvements in an amount not to exceed $715,669.10; (3) award a contract to the Orange
  County Conservation Corps, (OCCC) (A15-06) in an amount not to exceed $31,262.00
  for planting; and (4) adopt Resolution 15-08 Amending the Fiscal Year 2014–2015
  Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Project 221.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager Wilberg announced that staff has distributed an outline of the various public
services contracts that will be out for bid over the next several months. The contracts will be
coming to the City Council for approval beginning in May and bid specifications are currently
being prepared. He encouraged the City Council Members to contact staff if they have specific
concerns about any of the contracts or projects so that adjustments can be made before the RFPs
are issued.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

20.  Vector Control Trustee Responsibilities

City Council Minutes  6  February 16, 2015
   The City Council received the presentation from Vector Board Trustee Dave Leckness.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

14.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths presented the report.

15.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

16.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Due to Council Member Ury’s absence, there was no report given.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

18.  Demand to State to Cure Fire Map Misinformation

  Council Member Bucknum presented her report and asked her colleagues to approve the
  proposed letter to Senator Pat Bates and that all Council Members sign the letter.

  Council Member Sachs stated that the Council hasn't even decided about rescinding the
  past ordinance. He feels that this is a bit premature and it is out of the chain of command
  to include a State Senator in a local issue between the City, OCFA and CalFire. He thinks
  the City has to go through the OCFA Board and including the State does not provide an
  advantage for local control.

  By consensus, this matter was continued to the March 16, 2015, City Council Meeting.

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at recent events including the renaming of
Alicia Park to William S. Craycraft Park. She stated that it was a show of unity to see so many
prior Mayors, Council Members, Commissioners and Rotarians who joined together to honor not
only the opening day of girls softball, but the unveiling of the new park monument. She also
attended the Elks Club Law Enforcement and Firefighters Appreciation Awards ceremony and she
City Council Minutes  7  February 16, 2015
 thanked the Elks for hosting that event each year. Council Member Bucknum discussed her
attendance at the ribbon cutting ceremony for Driving Miz Daisy which is a vintage flea market
held on the 2nd Sunday of each month at Saddleback College. She also attended the grand opening
of the Mission Viejo Auto Club office, two ACC-OC meetings, a Government Innovation
Committee meeting, a city leadership reception at Angels Stadium and the City’s character movie,
The 99ers. Council Member Bucknum announced that the City will host the Rally for Life event
at the Marguerite Tennis Center on Sunday March 1 and she encouraged residents to sign up to
play tennis or to come out and watch. Check-in begins at 9:00 a.m. with the competition soon
thereafter and all proceeds from the event will benefit the American Cancer Society. Also on
March 1 the City’s Writers Present series will feature the Author and the Illustrator of the Fancy
Nancy series. Council Member Bucknum encouraged residents to visit CPK tonight before they
close as 20% of purchases will benefit the Honor Flight program. Presenting the front page of the
Saddleback Valley News, Council Member Bucknum noted that the paper features a list of local
students and the colleges that they have committed to and she expressed great pride in the kids
coming out Mission Viejo high schools. She also complimented the City’s reporter for doing a
feature on Pavion Park and in conclusion, Council Member Bucknum shared a quote from
Abraham Lincoln: "A house divided against itself cannot stand."

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he just completed the UCI Extension Public Policy
Making Course which was 4 Fridays of intense drilling down into the making of public
policy. He stated that it was a good seminar and participants were quizzed after each
event. Council Member Sachs recommend that his colleagues attend the policy making course
and he announced that the second level will be coming next year. He stated that he thought he
knew a lot before he was elected but he understands the public process even better now. Council
Member Sachs recounted that his neighbor came to him a few weeks ago expressing his desire
to volunteer for the City. He ended up meeting with Director Mark Nix and was asked to take a
look at the Potocki Center which seems to be a city asset that is not well used. His neighbor
presented a good report on his findings and Council Member Sachs noted that he will get a copy
to the City Clerk for the public record as there are interesting ideas that the City should consider
for utilizing the facility.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

19.  Establishing Compensation for City Board Members & Commissioners

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he will table this matter to a future meeting. He
  thanked the City's Commissioners for all of their hard work for just $50 a month and he
  noted that he is going to try and get the stipend raised to $100 a month.

City Council Minutes  8  February 16, 2015
 Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that he has been learning as much as he can about the fire maps
issue and he looks forward to the next meeting when it will be discussed again. He noted that he
is impressed with all the new businesses coming to town including the Driving Miz Daisy flea
market and the AAA grand opening. He thanked the Elks for rewarding fire and law enforcement
personnel with awards of excellence and discussed his attendance at the William S. Craycraft Park
renaming ceremony. Mayor Pro Tem Raths further announced that he recently toured the San
Onofre nuclear power plant and he is still trying to gather more information and he plans to report
back to Council sometime in the near future. He also attended the Municipal Water District of
Orange County policy meeting where the message was clear that the drought in Orange County is
real and is a very significant problem. Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that next week, on
February 23, the Marine Corps will celebrate the 70th Anniversary of the flag raising on Iwo
Jima. In honor of that, he will be hosting a luncheon, along with Laura Dietz, at the Newport
Marriott and he invited anyone who would like to attend to contact him at his city email
address. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Raths noted that he has heard complaints from residents that the
rear end of the dog statue at La Paws Park faces the road and he asked staff if the placement of the
statue can be adjusted.

Mayor Schlicht

21.  Change in City Council Meeting Time and Day

  Mayor Schlicht presented her report.

  Ron Ruef, Community Services Commissioner, M.V.: stated that it will be difficult for him
  to attend Community Services Commission meetings if they are moved to the third
  Tuesday of the month and he requested that they be moved to the third Monday of the
  month instead.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: recommended that the Council Meetings be moved to Tuesday to
  allow the Council Members additional time to review agenda materials.

  Helen Workun, M.V.: presented a written comment in opposition to changing the Council
  Meeting dates.

  Mayor Pro Tem Raths announced that prior to the Council Meeting, the City Clerk
  received 7 emails in favor of moving the meeting to Tuesdays and 4 emails in opposition.

  The Council Members discussed the merits and downsides to moving the meeting date and
  time and the effect a change would have on the public, the Council Members and staff.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to (1) move the City
  Council Meetings to the 2nd and 4th Tuesdays of the month at 5:00 p.m., effective August
  25, 2015, and move the distribution of the agenda to the City Council Members to the

City Council Minutes  9  February 16, 2015
   Thursday prior to the Tuesday Council Meeting; and (2) adopt Resolution 15-09, as
  amended, Establishing the Day and Times of Regular Meetings of the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Bucknum
  ABSENT:  Ury

22.  Request the Community Services Commission to Research Potential Youth Center
  Facilities and Programming Opportunities

  Mayor Schlicht presented the report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to direct the
  Community Services Commission to research potential youth center facilities and
  programming opportunities.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

23.  Request the Planning and Transportation Commission to Have the Traffic
  Committee Review Traffic Conditions in the City, Along with Different Traffic Flow
  Technologies to Help Reduce Traffic Congestion

  Mayor Schlicht presented the report.

  Motion made by Mayor Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Raths, to direct that the
  Planning and Transportation Commission have the Traffic Committee review traffic
  conditions in the City, along with different traffic flow technologies to help reduce traffic
  congestion; and direct the committee to return with a progress report within 90 days.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

Mayor Schlicht thanked her colleagues for the good discussions tonight and she stated that
reasonable minds can disagree as long as there are respectful discussions. She noted that she will
be giving the City Clerk a handout on the fire maps issue for the public record. Mayor Schlicht

City Council Minutes  10  February 16, 2015
 thanked VFW Post 6024 for leading the Council and audience in the flag salute and for coming to
the meeting to honor Home Town Hero, Admiral Bill Miles. She announced that she was honored
to be at two dinners in the last month to salute public servants and she missed not hearing bagpipes
at the Elks dinner where police and fire heroes were honored. She did however enjoy the bagpipe
performance at the police and fire Best and Bravest awards ceremony. Mayor Schlicht recounted
her fun in catching the first pitch from softball star Jenny Finch pitch and two weeks later, she was
honored to unveil the new monument for the renaming of Alicia Park to William S. Craycraft
Park. She noted that it was very moving to have Bill’s three sons in attendance. In closing, Mayor
Schlicht quoted President George Washington: "The Constitution is the guide which I will never
abandon," and President Abraham Lincoln: "Government of the people, by the people, for the
people, shall not perish from the Earth.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:00 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Schlicht adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 2, 2015, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November March 2, 2015

City Council Minutes  11  February 16, 2015
